terms.definition: The Moon passing directly between the Sun and Earth, briefly blocking sunlight from part of Earth's surface.
Earth passing directly between the Sun and the Moon, casting Earth's shadow onto the Moon.
The point where the Moon's tilted orbital path crosses Earth's orbital plane; eclipses can only happen when the Moon is near a node at New or Full Moon.
An eclipse where the alignment is close to perfect, so the shadow lands squarely on its target.
An eclipse where the alignment is close but not exact, so only part of the shadow reaches its target.
